_schema.passes: true | false | "blocked" — three states, because reality has three. `true` means every step was observed to pass. `false` means it failed or has not been attempted. `"blocked"` means the step is correct and this environment cannot execute it — a headless browser that cannot emulate a media query, a CI run that only fires on a pull request, a clipboard that needs real user activation. Recording those as `true` with an apology in `notes` is the exact fudge invariant 2 exists to prevent, and it is what happened before this field had a third state.
_schema.blocked_reason: Required when passes is "blocked". What specifically could not be observed, and why — the limitation, not the feature.
_schema.recheck_when: Required when passes is "blocked". The condition under which this becomes verifiable: 'a real browser with reduced motion enabled', 'once a PR is open'. Stage 4 collects these; a blocked feature with no recheck condition is an abandoned one.
_schema.notes: What was observed. Not what was intended.
